titulo: The dish you weren't going to order
subtitulo: Comida corrida, the fixed daily lunch nobody prints in English, and the two words that unlock it
cena: There's no menu on the table — just a chalkboard nobody's translated, and the smell of something that's clearly the reason everyone else in the room looks satisfied.
decisao: pedir a comida corrida do dia em vez de procurar o prato que você já conhece — o prato certo é o que a casa decidiu fazer hoje, não o que está traduzido
frasePiso: The best dish in the room is often the one with no name on an English menu, because there is no English menu — there's just today's comida corrida.

fatosDatados.afirmacao: Comida corrida (also called menú del día) is a fixed-price multi-course lunch — typically soup or starter, a main dish, rice or beans, and a drink — served at fondas roughly from midday to early afternoon, commonly in the 60-150 MXN range depending on the establishment.
fatosDatados.fonte: Consenso de guias gastronômicos (Monte Albán Heritage Center, My Slice of Mexico, CCRA Travel) — preços variam por cidade e casa

steps.pt: Some of the best food has no printed menu — just a chalkboard, or nothing, today's comida corrida decided that morning.

steps.es: Hoy tenemos comida corrida: sopa, guisado y agua.
steps.pt: Today we have comida corrida: soup, a stew, and a drink.
steps.tts: Hoy tenemos comida corrida: sopa, guisado y agua.

steps.pt: Comida corrida — like menú del día — is a full fixed lunch, fair price, a few hours around midday.

steps.promptPt: That's exactly what you want. Say you'll have the comida corrida. Speak now.
steps.es: Quiero la comida corrida, por favor.
steps.pinyin: KYEH-roh lah koh-MEE-dah koh-RREE-dah, por fah-BOR
steps.pt: I'd like the comida corrida, please.
steps.tts: Quiero la comida corrida, por favor.

steps.pt: Comida corrida still asks you to choose between two or three set options at each course. You don't need every word — you need one clean choice.

steps.promptPt: Pick one. Say soup. Speak now.
The main course also has two options. Choose chicken. Speak now.

steps.pt: When there's a longer menu and no comida corrida, this move unlocks the good dish instead of the safe one.

steps.promptPt: You're not sure what to get. Ask what they recommend. Speak now.

steps.pt: The mole is really good today.

steps.promptPt: You want the local thing, not the safe thing. Speak now.

steps.promptPt: Find out what the fixed price actually covers. Speak now.
Point and name, nothing more. Speak now.
steps.pt: Can I have the chicken one?

steps.promptPt: Say it before it is made, not after. Speak now.

aprofundar.titulo: The unwritten menu is often the good one

secoes.corpo: Because the menu is fixed by the kitchen each morning, asking hoy — 'what's today's comida corrida?' — is more useful than expecting the same dish twice.
Fondas typically serve comida corrida from around midday to mid-afternoon, tied to the comida hour from I01 — it usually isn't available in the evening.

secoes.titulo: Asking for a recommendation is not indecision
secoes.corpo: ¿Qué me recomienda? is a completely normal, common question — it signals trust in the kitchen, not that you couldn't read the menu.

permissao: You are allowed to order the thing you can't fully translate. Comida corrida and 'qué me recomienda' both work precisely because you don't need to know every word on the board — you need to trust the kitchen, which is the whole point.
espelho: Ordering 'whatever the chef recommends' or the unlabelled daily special at a local diner back home is the exact same move, just in a different language — nobody there thinks it's indecisive to trust the kitchen either.

fichasCulturais.sinal: You walk into a small fonda and there's no printed menu anywhere, just a chalkboard in Spanish and the smell of something you can't identify.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: This place isn't set up for someone who doesn't already know the food, or I should find somewhere with an English menu instead.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: Many of the best, most economical lunch spots in Mexico run entirely on comida corrida — a fixed daily menu decided that morning — and simply never print a translated menu because the whole model is built around trusting the kitchen's daily choice, not browsing options.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Ask hoy tenemos qué (what do you have today) or simply say quiero la comida corrida, and choose between the two or three options offered at each course.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: You get a full, freshly made meal at a fair price, often better than anything on a translated tourist menu nearby.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not in the evening or at more formal restaurants with an à la carte menu — comida corrida is specifically a midday, fonda-style institution.
